data.kora_index_explanation: KORA Index of 47 reflects a company in early-stage activation. Programs exist, budgets are allocated, and some workers are genuinely engaged — but the activation pattern is narrow. A small core of 12% of workers is generating 64% of measured impact. The broader workforce, particularly in operations, has minimal recorded participation beyond mandatory compliance events.
data.safeguard_explanation: The Activation Safeguard is WARNING because Activation Rate (AR = 0.38) falls below the CLEAR threshold of 0.40. Under OR logic, even one metric in the warning band is sufficient to trigger this status. The KORA Index remains available as a diagnostic output, but must be interpreted with reduced confidence given the limited participation base.
data.confidence_explanation: The Confidence Score of 60% reflects moderate data quality. HRIS records are complete, but the LMS export covers only 62% of events, and the welfare provider supplies manual files rather than API data. 29% of IMPACT events are self-declared without advisor review. These gaps reduce the reliability of the output and are reflected in the lower CS component value.

strong_components.label: Pillar Coverage
strong_components.explanation: Three pillars (LIFE, GROWTH, CONNECTION) have some meaningful participation. LIFE is strong due to safety compliance and wellbeing programs. GROWTH is supported by LMS activity.

strong_components.label: Normalized Intensity
strong_components.explanation: Workers who do participate tend to engage with reasonable intensity. The issue is breadth, not depth — the active minority contributes meaningfully.

weak_components.label: Worker Balance
weak_components.explanation: The most significant structural weakness. 64% of all Impact Units are generated by 12% of workers. The remaining 88% contribute very little. This signals a program that reaches only the already-engaged.

weak_components.label: Continuity
weak_components.explanation: Workers who engage in one period do not consistently return in the next. Only 28% of active workers show cross-period sustained engagement. Programs may be one-time events rather than sustained pathways.

weak_components.label: Equity
weak_components.explanation: The Operations department — 36% of the workforce — has an activation rate of only 11%. This site-level imbalance is the primary equity driver. Workers in plant environments are largely absent from KORA data.

weak_components.label: Pillar Balance
weak_components.explanation: LIFE accounts for 44% of all IU, mainly through safety compliance. CONNECTION and LEGACY are barely present. The program mix does not distribute engagement evenly across the human value pillars.

next_best_actions.detail: The Plant Bergamo cluster (90 workers, AR 11%) represents the largest single opportunity. Introduce accessible on-site LIFE and CONNECTION programs that do not require digital access. Even raising AR at this site to 30% would materially improve AR, EQ, and WB scores.

next_best_actions.action: Convert occasional users to sustained participants
next_best_actions.detail: 55 workers engage occasionally but do not return in consecutive periods. Structured continuity nudges, milestone recognition (via My KORA), or recurring accessible events could convert this group to cross-period participants.

next_best_actions.action: Increase verification coverage for IMPACT events
next_best_actions.detail: 29% of IMPACT events are self-declared without advisor review. Routing these through the advisor queue would significantly raise VR and increase confidence in the IMPACT pillar contribution.

The Mentoring Circle program exists but has low participation (14% AR). Structured senior-junior pairings with minimal time commitment could raise LEGACY and CONNECTION IU with targeted outreach to Administration and senior Sales workers.

data.kora_index_explanation: KORA Index of 64 reflects meaningful improvement across activation breadth, pillar balance, and verification quality. The Q4 period shows that acting on specific KORA recommendations can produce measurable change. Activation Rate crossed the CLEAR threshold. Operations engagement improved. More workers are returning across periods. The concentration problem is reducing but not eliminated.
data.safeguard_explanation: The Activation Safeguard is CLEAR because both AR (0.52 ≥ 0.40) and MAR (0.38 ≥ 0.30) meet the required thresholds. The KORA Index can now be interpreted with increased confidence as a meaningful diagnostic output.
data.confidence_explanation: Confidence Score of 72% reflects improved data quality from Q4 additions. LMS export is now complete. More IMPACT events have been advisor-reviewed. The welfare provider data is still manual but more comprehensive. LEGACY remains a gap — only 6% of IU in this pillar, making its component value less reliable.

strong_components.label: Activation Rate
strong_components.explanation: Crossed the CLEAR threshold. The Operations site improvement was the key driver — plant activation rose from 11% to 22%, adding meaningful breadth.

strong_components.label: Verification Rate
strong_components.explanation: Verification improved significantly. More events routed through advisor review. Self-declared IMPACT events now backed by evidence in majority of cases.

strong_components.label: Continuity
strong_components.explanation: Sustained engagement has improved — 44% of active workers showed cross-period participation. This suggests the Q4 programs have started to build habits rather than one-time events.

weak_components.label: Worker Balance
weak_components.explanation: Balance improved (from 0.29 to 0.51) but the top concentration pattern persists. Top active workers still generate a disproportionate share of IU. Continued broadening of activation is needed.

weak_components.label: Continuity
weak_components.explanation: Improved but still below 0.50. More than half of active workers are not yet sustaining engagement across multiple periods.

weak_components.label: Pillar Coverage
weak_components.explanation: LEGACY pillar remains barely present at 6% of IU. Without a structured LEGACY pathway — mentoring, knowledge transfer, senior contribution — this pillar will not improve.

next_best_actions.detail: LEGACY is the only pillar not showing meaningful progress. Structured knowledge-transfer programs, reverse-mentoring, or senior-contribution initiatives with verifiable outcomes could raise PC and PB further.
Plant Bergamo reached 22% AR in S2 — a significant jump from 11%. Sustaining this requires ongoing accessible programming and reducing operational barriers to participation.

next_best_actions.action: Convert occasional users to sustained participants via My KORA
next_best_actions.detail: My KORA milestone recognition and continuity tracking can increase the probability that occasional participants return in subsequent periods.
